Figure 5: (a) Running answer states across turns for GPT-5-mini under different shard counts (N = 4, 8, 12, 16). Figure 6: Distribution of lab-result cases by total turn count and by number of lab results.

Table 6: First-answer accuracy (%) under Ask Question First, broken down by disease and lab-result order. Results are shown for Early, Middle, and Late lab-result placement, with the number of turns fixed at 10. Bold disease names denote lab-dependent diseases.

Table 2: Comparison of model performance in the 9-turn setting. We report the average turn at which each model produces its first answer (µ ± σ), the abstention rate, the accuracy of the model’s initial answer (Ini.), the accuracy when all information is provided (Full), and the accuracy drop from Full to Ini. ∆.
Figure 1: Overview of MINT benchmark construction and evaluation settings.

Table 4: Answer-revision behavior across five medical benchmarks. FR denotes flip rate, T2F denotes true-to-false rate, F2T denotes false-to-true rate, and RR denotes restoration rate, computed as F2T/T2F, under the multi-turn Q-First setting. When T2F is 0, RR is N/A.

Figure 3: Proportion of Correct, Incorrect, and Hold responses across six turns for 11 models. For most models, hold responses decrease over turns while the proportion of correct answers increases by the final turn.

Figure 8: Representative behavioral patterns observed in Claude Sonnet 4.6. Left: Rush to Answer. (a) The model guesses at Turn 1 with no clinical context, and (b) it answers at an early turn with minimal information. Middle: Self-correction. The model initially answers incorrectly but revises to the correct option over subsequent turns. Right: Lure to Answer. The same question under two lab result placements (early vs. middle, marked with LAB badges); early placement triggers earlier responses. Green and red borders indicate correct and incorrect answers, respectively.

Figure 7: Representative response trajectories under different lab-result orders. For GPT-5mini on 10-turn cases, each row shows an example case trajectory when the key lab result is introduced early, middle, or late. Cells indicate whether the model gives no answer (N), a correct answer (T), or an incorrect answer (F) at each turn; outlined cells mark the turn where the lab result is revealed.

Figure 4: Effects of lab-result timing on response behavior and self-correction for GPT-5 mini in 10-turn cases. (a) Distribution of the first-answer turn under early, middle, and late lab-result placement, shown separately for lab-dependent and non-lab-dependent diseases. (b) Turn-level response composition for each lab-result order, showing correct, incorrect, and hold states across turns. (c) Heatmaps of False-to-True (left) and True-to-False (right) transitions by window size/turn gap, stratified by disease type and lab-result placement.

Table 1: Performance (%) under two single-turn settings, Full and Conc., and two multi-turn settings, Ask-Question-First (Q-First) and Ask-Question-Last (Q-Last). Under Q-First, we report Ini. (accuracy at the first turn where the model answers), Final (accuracy at the final turn after all evidence shards are revealed), and Abs. (abstention rate). Under Q-Last, we report Ans. (final-answer accuracy when the question is revealed only at the last turn). Conc. denotes the concatenated-shards single-turn input. Cell background color indicates the change relative to the same model’s Full setting: darker red indicates a larger decrease, and darker green indicates a larger increase.

Table 7: Overall performance (%) under different lab-result orders. Results are shown for Early, Middle, and Late lab-result placement. We report initial-answer accuracy, finalanswer accuracy, and abstention rate for Ask Question First, and final-answer accuracy and abstention rate for Ask Question Last.
